title: kate-lsp: turn a transaction into didChange events
summary: content_changes maps every edit of a transaction to one TextDocumentContentChangeEvent with a range in the pre-state text and the new text. The events are in descending start order so that each range stays valid after the earlier events apply. No diff and no full text resend.

lane.reason: A Cursor cloud agent codes this packet. The crate is pure Rust, the test runs a fake server over pipes on Linux, and the backlog marks the LSP client CLOUD.

definitions.definition:
/// One event per edit against `before`, last edit first.
pub fn content_changes(before: &kate_text::Rope, tx: &kate_text::Transaction, encoding: PositionEncoding) -> Vec<lsp_types::TextDocumentContentChangeEvent>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: For each edit in tx.edits() reversed, build the range from to_lsp(before, edit.start) and to_lsp(before, edit.old_end()), set range_length None, and text to edit.new. The test two_edits_become_two_events_last_first uses the rope ab\ncd with a transaction that inserts X at 0 and replaces d at 4 with YY, and asserts two events: the first has range line 1 character 1 to line 1 character 2 and text YY, the second has an empty range at line 0 character 0 and text X. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: sync::tests::two_edits_become_two_events_last_first
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because content_changes does not exist. After the change the later edit comes first and each range is in pre-state positions.
